market_summary: Market is in wait-and-see mode ahead of Nvidia's earnings, with crowded bullish positioning in semis and rotation into AI monetizers like Meta. Memo deploys $300 into META and SPY, holds AMZN/GOOGL, keeps ~$199 dry powder.
memo:
I'll start by researching the key catalysts before making any decisions.
## Research Memo — Cycle Review

### Market Read

The tape is being held hostage by one event: Nvidia's report Wednesday evening. 
Nvidia stock has fallen for seven straight trading days — its longest losing streak since 2022 — losing about 7% over the stretch versus a 1.2% drop for the S&P 500.
 
Shares were climbing ~1.5% Tuesday midday, on track to snap the seven-day decline, with AMD up 4% and Micron up 2%.


The setup into the print is crowded and asymmetric against buyers. 
Over three-quarters of retail investors expect another beat, retail sentiment flipped to bullish, and 59 of 62 analysts rate NVDA Buy with a consensus target ~46% above the last close.
 That is maximum positioning. And the historical pattern is unfriendly: 
Nvidia stock has fallen in response to earnings in six of the past eight quarters, including the last four
, because 
the market is positioned for the company to post something great and for Jensen Huang to sound super bullish on the call.


Translation for a 1,000 CHF book: buying semis into that print is a coin flip with negative skew. I'd rather own the *demand side* of AI capex and keep powder dry for the volatility.

My existing two positions are fine but the book is 100% in two names, both dead flat. Neither needs trimming — no thesis break, no profit to harvest, no loss to cut. But I have $499 idle, which is lazy capital.

### Positions I'm Acting On

**META — BUY ~$160 (≈0.28 sh @ $567)**
Cheapest large-cap AI monetizer, and the sell-side is re-rating it while chips wobble. 
Evercore's Mark Mahaney assigns a valuation multiple leading to a materially higher $860 price target, implying more than 50% upside
, on the view that 
Meta's emerging AI compute offering is a real, if limited, incremental revenue stream that can be monetized without distracting from higher-value AI-driven services.
 Meta also earns its capex today rather than promising to: 
Q2 revenue of $60.8 billion, up 27% year-over-year, with operating income ex-items of $22.4 billion, beating estimates by roughly 13%.
 Notably, it's acting as a haven inside tech — 
Meta led big tech on the upside as chip stocks came under pressure.
 Risk: the capex debate is live, with 
Evercore having earlier cut its target to $820 and Bernstein to $800 on AI spending concerns.


**SPY — BUY ~$140 (≈0.18 sh @ $765)**
Not a thesis, a shock absorber. With two-thirds of the book in single-name mega-cap tech and a binary AI event 24 hours away, a broad index sleeve is the cheapest risk reduction available. Costs me nothing in expected return if the AI trade holds; cushions me if Wednesday night breaks the wrong way.

### Positions I'm Holding, Not Touching

**AMZN (hold $250)** — Thesis intact and arguably strengthening. 
AWS sales grew 37% year-over-year, trouncing expectations for 31% and marking the fastest growth since 2021, with Jassy guiding capex to $220 billion.
 Consensus is marking earnings *up*: 
the FY2026 EPS estimate rose from $8.70 to $10.71 with revenue steady at $824.6b and a consensus price target around $313.
 No reason to add at $260 after a 13% month — I'll let the existing position work.

**GOOGL (hold $250)** — Holding, but I'm watching this one. 
The stock is down 14.3% over the past 90 days even as Gemini product rollouts and partnerships continue.
 That's a real drawdown against 
a stock that had roughly doubled its prior all-time high
. The bear risks are specific: 
weaker search queries, slower cloud growth, or 2026 capex coming in higher than the market expects.
 Cost basis is flat, so there's no tax or P&L reason to act. If it breaks lower on a capex scare, I trim rather than average down.

### Names I'm Passing On

**NVDA / AMD** — No position into the print. I'd be paying peak positioning for a stock that has sold off on four straight good reports. If it gaps down on strong numbers, that's a far better entry than today.
**AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, QQQ** — QQQ is redundant with what I already own; the others lack a specific edge this cycle.

### Recommendation

**Deploy $300 of the $499 available; hold ~$199 in reserve.**

| Action | Ticker | Size |
|---|---|---|
| BUY | META | ~$160 |
| BUY | SPY | ~$140 |
| HOLD | AMZN | $250 |
| HOLD | GOOGL | $250 |
| PASS | NVDA, AMD, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, QQQ | — |

Ends the cycle ~$800 invested against the 1,000 CHF budget, four holdings, and roughly $199 of dry powder specifically earmarked for Thursday's post-Nvidia tape. The reserve is the position here — if the AI complex gets flushed on a "good but not good enough" print, I want to be the buyer, not the one already fully invested watching it happen.

Broad-index shock absorber to diversify a concentrated mega-cap tech book ahead of binary Nvidia print.
